ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/exr: Round dc_w/h up

Without rounding them up there are too few dc coeffs for the blocks.
We do not know if this way of handling odd dimensions is correct, as we have
no such DWA sample.
thus we ask the user for a sample if she encounters such a file

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: BIGSLEEP-445392027-crash.exr

Found-by: Google Big Sleep
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: The fix addresses an out-of-bounds read in the EXR DWA decompression path. The root cause is that dc_w/dc_h were computed with a truncating shift (xsize >> 3) instead of ceiling division, while the decode loop iterates over the full block grid including partial trailing blocks. I applied the exact same two changes as the fix commit: (1) changed dc_w/dc_h computation to round up via (x + 7) >> 3, and (2) added an avpriv_request_sample() call warning when xsize/ysize aren't multiples of 8, placed at the equivalent logical point in this codebase's version of dwa_uncompress (after the compressed_size bounds check, before bytestream2_init is called to start parsing the compressed streams). The surrounding code in this snapshot lacks some checks present in later ffmpeg versions (e.g., ac_size<=0, rle_raw_size>INT_MAX), but those are unrelated to this fix and were not part of the required change, so I left them alone to keep the diff minimal and scoped to the actual vulnerability fix.
